(As someone who's taken Latin: the adjective alter ends in -er in the masculine nominative singular, so the comparative is alterior, not alterius.)

I just really don't think you should create a new object class (especially without explaining it). So far, literally every single SCP I've seen follows the object classes that are predefined and nigh-universally agreed upon; I don't think you should stray from that convention "just to sound cool." item.content:encoded:
I've reworked the first sentence of the description to mention herbivory, which is specifically the consumption of plants. Other plants consume plant matter, yes, but in the form of absorbing nutrients from the soil, which is something else entirely.

The object class is unexplained because I never really bothered to write up a formal explanation for this style. 'Alterius' is Latin for 'other', and I used it because it alluded to the extradimensional properties of the SCP. It's honestly just there to sound cool and get people talking.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I've got an issue with the object class… Not only are you creating an entirely new class (sub-class, but that's just semantics), but you're failing to explain how it differs from existing classes. In addition, this sentence, "SCP-824 is a species of tree that is characterized by significant mobility and consumes plant matter," bothers me… Technically, ALL plants consume plant matter. I feel like it could be better rewritten as "SCP-824 is a species of tree that is characterized by its significant mobility and the means by which it consumes plant matter," or better yet, "the means by which it obtains its nutrients." (Given that the method of consumption isn't the only anomaly; it's also anomalous that it actively seeks and draws in plant matter to consume, I don't feel like just saying that its consumption methods are all that are anomalous.)

item.content:encoded: I'm not 100% sure what you're asking, but SCP-████ does not (at this time; for all I know, someone could write it) exist on the site. The deal is that SCP-████ is probability-affecting — it managed to grow eight anomalous species and lack any sort of pathogens or bugs. 824 evolved within that environment. The probability affecting meant that, when faced with kudzu, 824 was able to evolve some rather unusual adaptations to deal with that threat.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Does it consume things made out of plant matter, like pencils, paper and cotton cloth?

Don't see why not.

What exactly is the point of having two different types of the same tree? Why not just focus on either the ones from the extra-dimensional pocket or from the Japanese island?

The part with the extradimensional ones is to sort of give them an origin story. The ones on the island are to show that they can somehow be turned into something suitable for agriculture.

Why has the Foundation not simply seized these trees and administered amnesiacs?

Because A) They've been living with these trees for a long time, and so long as they maintain secrecy operations, they don't have to disrupt normalcy for the people on the island. Much like the existence of anomalies would turn most of the world on its head, the lack of these trees would turn these people's lives over. And, B) They want to try and figure out how the trees got here and how they got turned from indiscriminate nomming machines to apple-picking trees.
